title: Service and Process Management knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under “Service and Process Management”?
options: Checking whether a process is running
questions.answer_key: Checking whether a process is running
questions.explanation: The supplied Bash.pdf curriculum lists “Checking whether a process is running” under lesson 177, “Service and Process Management”. Review the topic in the lesson content to connect the term with its practical use.

questions.prompt: Which approach is the strongest default when applying “Service and Process Management”?
options: Preview high-impact changes, verify results, and document recovery.
Assume that a working happy-path example proves correctness for every input.
Evaluate constructed user-controlled strings as shell commands to reduce parsing code.
Skip version checks because all common environments provide the same Bash features.
questions.answer_key: Preview high-impact changes, verify results, and document recovery.
questions.explanation: Preview high-impact changes, verify results, and document recovery. This approach keeps assumptions visible and makes results verifiable.

questions.prompt: Which practice best prevents a common reliability or maintenance error related to “Service and Process Management”?
options: Treat one successful output as proof that the workflow is safe in production.
Track task lifecycles, define cleanup on normal exit and interruption, and collect each status.
Assume the command behaves the same across all versions and operating systems.
Skip invalid inputs because the example uses trusted sample data.
questions.answer_key: Track task lifecycles, define cleanup on normal exit and interruption, and collect each status.
questions.explanation: Track task lifecycles, define cleanup on normal exit and interruption, and collect each status. The appropriate checks depend on the target environment and should be reviewed before publishing a script.
